title: References of the land
preface: A tale refers. These are the rooms, creatures, objects, and rumours it points at without stopping for.

inWhich.1: a dog finds an egg the maps will not admit
inWhich.2: the grove answers a beat late, and will not swear to it
inWhich.3: two roads claim the same step
inWhich.4: keys are filed smaller, and none of them fit
inWhich.5: two slips try to be one harvest
inWhich.6: glass shows a light it does not own
inWhich.7: an oath is paid in fruit
inWhich.8: water keeps a face without stealing it
inWhich.9: the ninth honk is missing, and warms
inWhich.10: a hall tells the truth with its weight
inWhich.11: a garden blooms before its seed arrives
inWhich.12: rivers meet and remember their names
inWhich.13: the last door is shaped like a shell, and stays open

entries.title: The unnamed egg
entries.note: Warm where it ought to have been cold. No nest. No mother. The maps will not write it down. Carry it if you must; naming it is a kind of debt.

entries.title: Boof
entries.note: A dog. She works for fruit. She trusts a scent that ends in something real, and is suspicious of applause.

entries.title: Boonberries
entries.note: Ordinary magic: fruit, lantern-fuel, seed, and supper. Now and then one of them notices the story it is sitting in, which is more than most fruit will do.

entries.title: The Commons Scale
entries.note: Where the harvest is counted in public. A scale that belongs to the commons, not to a landlord. Intact seals have been known to lie.

entries.title: The maps that look away
entries.note: Boon.land's records hold only what the world has agreed exists. Ink that beads and will not take is not a metaphor. It is a refusal.

entries.title: The Grove of Echoes
entries.note: A thicket that replays testimony. Workers will not name it after dark. An echo is a summons, not evidence, which has disappointed several clerks.

entries.title: Crosswind Council
entries.note: Boon and bane sit under one weather. Keys may be filed smaller. They may not be grown while the room is asleep.

entries.title: A slip
entries.note: The paper a turn leaves behind. Two slips for one harvest cannot both post. A false slip is refused, which is how you know the walk means it.

entries.title: Lantern glass
entries.note: Bonk City's lanterns show light. They are not the light. Confusing the pane with the flame has started several small fires, all of them rhetorical.

entries.title: The market stone
entries.note: An oath is public. The fruit is private. The egg, if present, is the witness, and does not sign.

entries.title: The Watering Eye
entries.note: A well that folds a face without stealing it. Water keeps what you put in. It will not call it yours.

entries.title: The ninth honk
entries.note: Eight were sounded. The ninth was not. Its shard, if you believe the ridge, is warm and egg-shaped. No single keeper can hold the whole call.

entries.title: Bone.land
entries.note: The chassis. Joints exposed on purpose. A hall that would rather bonk you than flatter you. Plaster stories do not last here.

entries.title: The Boonberry Fool
entries.note: A spirit of wonder who keeps the town from growing too tidy. Often upside down. Rarely helpful in the way one hopes.

entries.title: A cell keeps its own law
entries.note: What remains the same under every honest test. The egg is one. The maps are not its jurisdiction.

entries.title: A key files smaller
entries.note: Permission may be narrowed. It may not be secretly widened. Brass that grows teeth overnight is a crime and a joke.

entries.title: A turn is admitted, or not
entries.note: Two routes that want the same next step must post as one. The sand is particular about this.

entries.title: The Scriptorium
entries.note: Where chambers are seeded, revised, and set on a calendar of stones. Patron seals buy presence, not rewrite rights.
